description: Splat resolution driven by camera-distance zoom (Esri-style scale in/out) instead of inheriting the mesh chunk's fixed zoom
wave_rationale: User 2026-07-12: splats 'still very low res' after round-3 jitter/overlap polish (terrain_splat_view_20260711 phase 1). User explicitly prioritized this (tile/LOD zoom pipeline) over marching-squares-style splat interpolation as the first fix to attempt.
outcome: 2026-07-12: implemented (LOD zoom + coverage-driven hole-fill) but REVERTED. The live coverage fill is O(n^2) per sub-tile and ran synchronously in reconcile_splat_chunks every time chunks bake; a zoom-in burst spiked frame time / allocator and CRASHED the app. Work pruned from feat/terrain-maps-fe-sync-iroh035-finish (reset to 473eed9); full implementation preserved on branch archive/splat-coverage-experiment-20260712 (commits 9839094 + 4be8ec4).
future_direction: User-chosen fix (2026-07-12): BAKE splat coverage into the hexon file ahead of time — precompute the filled/dense splat buffer once when the hexon/tileset is built, store it in the hexon format, and load it directly at runtime with NO live fill. This removes the per-frame client CPU cost entirely. A fresh track should implement: (1) hexon-format field for baked splat coverage, (2) an offline/build-time bake step that runs the coverage hole-fill once, (3) runtime load path that reads the baked buffer instead of computing. The reverted interpolate.rs coverage-fill algorithm (gap-sized, logarithmic-shrink, seam-guarded) is the correct ALGORITHM to run at bake time — see archive branch.
notes: Research (2026-07-12) confirmed CompositeTileSource is stateless-per-call and coordinate-driven — it already supports fetching any zoom on demand (fe-terrain/src/tiles/composite.rs); nothing pins it to one zoom. The only reason splats inherit the mesh chunk's zoom today is that reconcile_splat_chunks (fe-terrain/src/splat/render.rs:119-181) reuses chunk.tile_coords verbatim instead of computing its own camera-distance-aware desired zoom. This significantly de-risks the track: it's zoom-selection decoupling + a fetch-at-higher-zoom path, not a new fetch pipeline.
